summary: Lessons from twenty years running a small landscaping business, written as self-help for young people starting out. The member has already written two chapters herself; the agent must keep both exactly as they are and only plan around them.

memories.title: The first mower
memories.body: Bought a used push mower for $40 at a yard sale and made flyers at the library: June Mows, $15 a lawn. I was twenty-two and had exactly three customers by July.

memories.title: The Ochoa lawn
memories.body: Mowed the Ochoa place, an acre and a half on a slope, for $15. It took four hours. Mrs. Ochoa paid me $25 and said, charge what it costs you, honey.

memories.title: Saying the price out loud
memories.body: I practiced saying forty-five dollars in the truck mirror before every estimate. The first time I said it to a customer without flinching, he just said okay. That was the whole fight.

memories.title: The wall that fell down
memories.body: Built my first stone retaining wall and it collapsed in the first big rain. I rebuilt it for free over two weekends. The client hired me for three more jobs because of how I handled it.

memories.title: Saying no to Fairmont
memories.body: Turned down a contract with the Fairmont office park because they paid in 120 days. Everyone said I was crazy. Two other crews took it and one went under waiting for the checks.

memories.title: The notebook of every bid
memories.body: Started writing down every bid: what I quoted, what it actually took, what I'd charge next time. That notebook taught me more than any class.

memories.title: The recession winter
memories.body: Half my customers cancelled that fall. I kept the crew busy pulling buckthorn for the county at cost, just to keep everyone paid. We came out of it with the county as a customer.

memories.title: Hiring Marcus
memories.body: Hired Marcus Teague, nineteen, who showed up to the interview with his own gloves. I paid him more than I could afford because I wanted him to stay. He stayed eleven years.

memories.title: Marcus runs a crew
memories.body: Gave Marcus his own crew and his own truck. The first week I drove past his job sites three times a day. The second week I made myself stop.

memories.title: Asleep at a stoplight
memories.body: Worked ninety-hour weeks through the fall and fell asleep at a stoplight. Nobody was hurt. The next Monday I hired an office manager and stopped answering calls after six.

memories.title: Selling to Marcus
memories.body: Sold Halvorsen Yard & Stone to Marcus for a fair price, paid over five years. He kept the name. I still stop by the shop on Fridays with doughnuts.

memories.title: Office Wi-Fi
memories.body: Changed the office Wi-Fi password. The new one is on the sticky note under the printer.
